decision: Recommend removing Cargo96 at the frozen shipping protocol: writer reservation supersedes its intended concurrent dirty-to-fresh benefit. Native paired expectations are equivalent with retained known failures.

source.extra_tests_original_expectations: two compiler invocations; no Fresh shortcut for forced fix or environment-dependent inputs

source_reachability.admission: fine-grain immutable shared-registry Build/Check non-proc-macro library without dependencies
source_reachability.proof: All admitted units are reservation units. Canonical whole-graph leases precede observations; dirty writers restart with exclusive leases before fingerprint invalidation. Reserved unlock/lock/downgrade keep mode. Another compliant same-physical-key Cargo writer cannot finish between dirty preparation and the queued recheck.
source_reachability.scope: No intended natural concurrent other-producer dirty-to-fresh opportunity under frozen shipped reservation protocol. Callback execution itself is not declared unreachable.

limitations: All three native failures are retained and matched; this is paired expectation equivalence, not wholly green shared-cache coverage.
Approved prose says 67 shared cases; actual fixed018 harness has 69, including two original safety tests, and all expectations were unchanged.

RUST_LOG does not activate pinned Cargo CARGO_LOG debug tracing. Initial leaf fingerprints, actual rustc argv and artifact statuses independently show zero successful dirty-to-fresh leaf reuse; absent debug phrases do not establish universal recheck/provider invocation counts. Corrected logging probe is separate corroboration.

Writer-reservation reasoning assumes compliant actors respecting the same canonical unit locks. It does not cover noncooperating writers, unusual filesystem/freshness discrepancies, every configuration, or future locking changes.
Three Windows .bat checkout files use CRLF while Git blobs use LF; all Rust/config/manifest/lock bytes match and the Linux Cargo check does not use these activator scripts.

Full build/training provenance remains a separate accepted dependency. Runtime/native-test binary hashes are archived remote checks, not newly executed or rehashed remote binaries. No timing or protocol/report modifications were performed.
